articles.title: Netflix’s 'Kpop Demon Hunters' Replacement Reimagines a Classic Disney Princess
articles.summary: Alyce Tzue always loved fairy tales, but growing up as the only Asian kid in a homogeneous community in New Jersey, she worried she would never find her happily ever after. Instead of seeing herself in Cinderella, Tzue wondered why her stepsisters didn’t get their own magic.
body: "There really is no one Cinderella story," Ripa told Polygon in an interview at Annecy Festival. "A Chinese version introduced the stepmother, and the Italian version introduced the stepsisters."
Steps brings all that history together and gives it a modern update.
"There are certain things the audience wants to see. We were able to take some of these iconic canon moments and give it a little twist and show it from every perspective."

Steps follows Cinderella’s misunderstood stepsister Lilith (Ali Wong). After watching the Fairy Godmother (Bette Midler) give Cinderella (Amanda Seyfried) a dress, carriage, and glass slippers, Lilith tries to get some magic of her own. She accidentally turns her sister Margot (Stephanie Hsu) into a frog, causing chaos in the kingdom.

articles.title: What we've been playing - "I don't think this is this game's biggest problem"
articles.summary: Hello and welcome back to our regular feature where we write a little about the games we've been playing. This week, Kelsey takes solace in assassination; Connor revisits a foundational Korean MMO; Chris has some more thoughts about Marvel's Wolverine; Bertie tries to get to the end of Big Walk and…
body: Here's another question: do you remember what you were playing last week? You don't have to! The What We've Been Playing archive has you covered.

It's been a whirlwind few weeks so I've decided to sit down with a comfort game of mine: Hitman World of Assassination. Don't ask me why I find stepping into the shoes of Agent 47 comforting, because I don't really know. I guess there's something about exploring the likes of Berlin, Dartmoor, and Hokkaido and looking for new assassination opportunities - like killing off corporate baddies with an explosive rubber duck and pretending you had nothing to do with it - that I find incredibly satisfying. I mean, that's no doubt what IOI was going for.
In preparation for the release of MapleStory Classic World - a revival of the original MapleStory from back in my childhood - I downloaded and booted up the modern iteration of the 2D Korean MMO.

I was totally lost. That game has truly evolved over the past decade or so, unsurprisingly. It was a strange feeling, like returning to your home town and realising that it's true, the world really does continue to change even when you're not there to see it happen.

articles.title: Stephen King's Next Book is the Long-Awaited Conclusion To A 42-Year-Old Trilogy
articles.summary: There aren't many parts of Stephen King 's bibliography that you can realistically call "obscure." As one of the most famous novelists on Earth, and perhaps the single most famous living horror novelist, even King's lesser-known works are usually best-sellers.
body: However, King has dug into his back catalog for his next release. Other Worlds Than These, due out on Oct. 6, is the second sequel to The Talisman, a 1984 horror/fantasy novel that King wrote in collaboration with the late Peter Straub ( Ghost Story, Mr. X ).

Upon Other Worlds Than These 's release, it will have been just over 25 years since the previous installment in what’s now become a trilogy. As the title suggests, this is related to King's Dark Tower series, albeit a little distantly. If you're a fan of those books but aren't familiar with The Talisman, perhaps because you weren't yet born when it was released, this is your window to get caught up before Other Worlds Than These drops.

articles.title: Brandon Sanderson's Mistborn Expansion for the Cosmere RPG Is Up for Preorder at Amazon
articles.summary: Brandon Sanderson and Brotherwise Games have been hard at work producing Cosmere tabletop games since 2020. In addition to board games, the first core rulebooks for a full-on Cosmere RPG launched just last year after a very successful crowdfunding campaign.
body: The Mistborn Handbook, Campaign Guide, and Welcome to Scadriel guide are available to buy at Amazon with a November 4 release date.

The Mistborn Handbook is the main thing you'll need if you want to build characters in either era of Mistborn. You'll also get some general guidance for GMs building out a campaign in the world of Scadriel. Since it is a Mistborn game, there's also a focus on the metallic arts of allomancy and ferochemy you wouldn't get from the Stormlight characters.

While the handbook is essential for the basics of the RPG, you'll still need the campaign guide to insert your characters into a realistic setting from the books. You can choose to play a campaign through two different Eras, with consequences that 'echo across the centuries'. Your campaign through Mistborn Era 1 is designed to be played through levels 3-6 while Era 2 is designed for levels 3-9.

articles.title: GTA 6 Reviews Plague Real-Life Nudist Resort After Fans Draw Comparisons to Leaks
articles.summary: Grand Theft Auto 6 fans believe its nudist resort was inspired by a real-life location, and its owners are already being bombarded with problematic reviews. As if there was ever any doubt, GTA 6 fans are all over Rockstar Games' new video game.
body: Fans tracking down the locations behind some of their favorite video game levels is nothing new; Arc Raiders fans did something similar in January. But where the sleuthing for some games has often resulted in real-world positivity, Cypress Cove Nudist Resort isn't enjoying the increased visibility brought by GTA 6.

"For anyone wondering about the suddenly recurring references to 'Jason Duval,' 'Lucia,' binoculars, a pool, firearms, and other suspiciously similar details — those are references to Grand Theft Auto VI," the site owner said in response to just one of the many reviews that have shown up on the Cypress Cove Nudist Resort Google page recently. "Yes. A video game."

The owner, which has already taken what action it can against the reviews, said the influx of reviews is a "coordinated series of fabricated posts using GTA VI references." They then allege that some posts were followed by requests that the rest "pay money to have the reviews changed or removed."

articles.title: Alienware Just Released the World's First 39" 5K Monitor With RGB Stripe Tandem OLED Technology
articles.summary: Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology." You can finally get your hands on one. The new Alienware AW3926QW has just been listed at Dell for $1,099.99 with free delivery (10% less if you have a verified student account).
body: The Alienware AW3926QW has no lack of features that make it stand out from the crowd, but perhaps its most impressive technology is the RGB stripe tandem OLED panel. Tandem OLED stacks multiple OLED layers on top of each other instead of a single layer. Tandem OLED is better than other OLED panels because: 1) it's much brighter (the AW3926QW in particular has a very impressive 1,300 nits of peak brightness) and 2) it's less prone to burn-in.

The AW3926QW doubles down on this with new RGB stripe technology. Whereas traditional tandem OLEDs use white pixels, RGB stripe tandem OLED breaks the color down further into vertically aligned red, green, and blue pixels. This reduces color fringing and in turn significantly improves text clarity. It goes without saying that there are obvious benefits here for both gaming and productivity purposes alike.
points: Earlier this year, Dell announced the "world's first 39" 5K monitor with RGB stripe tandem OLED technology.

articles.title: GTA 6 Developer Is Fighting Drones And Hackers To Keep The Game’s Secrets Safe
articles.summary: As the studio behind one of the most highly anticipated games of all time, GTA 6 developer Rockstar Games has divulged more details on how it keeps its secrets. As part of a hearing, which began yesterday at the Glasgow Employment Tribunal--in which Rockstar Games has been accused of unlawfully…
body: "Guarding the secrets of the unique gameplay and design are akin to Apple protecting the iPhone or Coke protecting its formula," Rockstar said in its opening note (via IGN ). "The standards and expectations regarding information security and privacy are exponentially beyond that of most employers."

The company claims that people are so hell-bent on peeking behind the curtain that it was forced to coat its building windows with a privacy film after aerial drones were used to spy on employees and photograph the inside of the building. Because of that, Rockstar has had to implement numerous security measures, such as enforcing strict no-photography rules for visitors, banning external storage devices on office premises, and restricting remote work for employees. The developer also has a full-time team of five investigators and a director who keep an eye out for potential leaks.

articles.title: EA’s New Owners May Be Considering An Even Bigger Gaming Empire
articles.summary: EA has officially been sold, and with Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund now the majority shareholder in the video game company, talks are reportedly underway to merge it with Savvy Games Group, the gaming and esports holding company that's also owned by the PIF.
body: Speaking to Bloomberg, sources said the PIF is aiming to foster "better coordination" between its gaming assets, and the merger could happen once it completes its plan to acquire Chinese mobile gaming company Moonton, a deal valued at $6 billion. The PIF also owns Pokemon Go developer Scopely and game publisher SNK, and it holds sizable stakes in video game publishers like Nintendo, Capcom, and Koei Tecmo.

The move could face scrutiny from regulators across the globe, however, as this would place several of the biggest gaming franchises in the world under one roof, including EA Sports FC, Battlefield, and mobile juggernauts like Monopoly Go. While EA's acquisition is valued at $55 billion, the massive leveraged buyout has also saddled the game company with billions of debt that needs to be addressed.

The PIF is the majority owner of EA Games, with a 93.4% stake in the company, while its partners Silver Lake and Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner's private equity firm, Affinity Partners, own 5.5% and 1.1% of the company, respectively.

articles.title: After Sony tells fans they don't own digital games, one Consumer Rights group is tracking all the times PlayStation said the opposite
articles.summary: Last month, Sony argued that "reasonable consumers" already know they don't really own the digital goods they paid for. The Consumer Rights wiki has now made a list collecting more than 30 examples where Sony told customers they do, in fact, own the digital games they paid for.
body: A class action lawsuit recently filed against Sony alleged the PlayStation Store isn't clear enough about the fact that digital purchases don't equal digital ownership. Once a player makes a purchase on the PlayStation Store, they're paying for a digital license that's revocable at any point in time - the purchase doesn't guarantee you'll have access to a particular game or DLC or cosmetic pack forever.
One of the more recent examples can be found in Marvel's Wolverine's FAQ section: "Standard Edition owners can also upgrade to the Digital Deluxe Edition content."

The lawsuit claimants said Sony was in breach of a California Law that made it "unlawful for a seller of a digital good to advertise or offer for sale a digital good to a purchaser with the terms 'buy,' 'purchase,' or any other term which a reasonable person would understand to confer an unrestricted ownership interest in the digital good." (Reasonability doesn't seem like something you could measure in court, but I digress.) A digital vendor can get around the law by giving customers clear information about the licenses they're paying for. We'll see how the suit plays out over the coming weeks and months.
points: Last month, Sony argued that "reasonable consumers" already know they don't really own the digital goods they paid for.

articles.title: Switch 2 Update Secretly Makes Digital Game Sharing Much Better
articles.summary: Everyone is focused on VRR (variable refresh rate) support for Switch 2 while docked. But the latest system update just provided a notable quality-of-life improvement for people--especially families--who own multiple Switch 2 and Switch consoles.
body: For example, say your child is playing Super Mario Bros. Wonder on your old Switch OLED, but you want to play it on your Switch 2. You both can actually play the title simultaneously by turning off Wi-Fi on the original hybrid console. Then, on your Switch 2, you can utilize an online license to jump around as the mustached plumber, too. We tested this out successfully.

This also helps a lot between manually sending virtual game cards back and forth between Switch and Switch 2 systems. Now I can just start say, Blasphemous, on either system without having to actually send it from the previous place to a new one. Sure, it's not as smooth as using apps across Apple devices, but it's a step in the right direction.

Here's Nintendo's official language for the version 23.0.0 update, which incorporates Switch 2 and Switch. "When starting software, if a virtual game card cannot be ejected from another console because it is powered off or otherwise not connected to the internet, there will be a prompt to start the software using an online license."
points: Everyone is focused on VRR (variable refresh rate) support for Switch 2 while docked.

videos.title: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 Review
videos.summary: Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 reviewed by Will Borger on PC, also available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
body: "Fireteam Elite 2 doesn’t reinvent the wheel. It’s best alongside three friends for a full squad, but it’s fun enough solo as well. The story isn’t anything to write home about, but the characters are likeable, the missions are fun, and the new Specialist class provides a cool way to further customize your kit. There are some bugs in this bug hunt, but they don’t distract from the action too much. Turns out blasting Xernos and synths is a good time with friends, and there is a lot of blasting to be done thanks to the Horde mode and a smart unlockable system that encourages you to replay levels, explore each class, and try new things. It may not quite be a glorious day in the corps, but it’s damn close."
